patch.value: Fix daily release ordering so npm publish no longer races ahead of the protected main push

The release workflow published to npm before pushing the version bump to the protected main branch. Branch protection rejected git push origin HEAD:main with GH006 and set -e killed the job before the tag push, leaving npm at 2026.8.10 while main stayed at 2026.8.7 with no v2026.08.10 tag. Port the protected-PR merge flow from pm-context so main is advanced through a rebase PR before npm publish, and improve the merge wait to attempt the merge directly instead of polling mergeStateStatus, which deadlocked on BLOCKED with an empty statusCheckRollup.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Root cause: release.yml published to npm then pushed HEAD:main and the tag in one set -e block. main is protected so HEAD:main is rejected with GH006 and the tag push never runs, leaving npm ahead of git. Fix: merge the release metadata through a protected rebase PR before publishing, verify the merged commit, then publish with an idempotence guard and push the tag only. The merge wait attempts the merge directly and lets GitHub be the authority, resolving unresolved review threads first so advisory bot comments do not block required_conversation_resolution.

patch.value: Release workflow rewritten to merge release metadata through a protected rebase PR before npm publish, verify the merged commit, then publish with an idempotence guard and push the tag only. The merge wait attempts the merge directly via the GitHub merge API instead of polling mergeStateStatus, resolving unresolved review threads before each attempt.
Release workflow merges release metadata through a protected rebase PR before npm publish, verifies the merged commit, then publishes with an idempotence guard and pushes the tag only
A daily release advances main through a protected PR, publishes to npm only after the merge is verified, and pushes the release tag; a previously published version reconciles instead of failing

value.author: claude
value.text: Greptile reviewed the first version and reported that creating the release pull request with GITHUB_TOKEN suppresses its pull_request event so CI never starts. Measured against pm-changelog, the event is not suppressed: a CI run was created at 04:54:24Z with event pull_request for release branch release/2026.8.9. The real blocker is that attempt 1 concluded action_required, meaning the run was parked awaiting workflow approval under the fork pull request contributor approval policy of first_time_contributors, and github-actions had no merged pull request in that repository yet. A human re-ran it at 05:36Z, twelve minutes after the release had already timed out.

value.author: claude
value.text: Added detection for runs parked on action_required. The merge wait now reports the run URL, attempts to approve it with the actions write permission, and the deadline error distinguishes awaiting approval from a failed required check, so a stalled release is diagnosable immediately instead of after thirty minutes of empty status rollups.

value.author: claude
value.text: Round two review fixes. CodeRabbit found that the Push release tag step consulted only the local tag database, while the last tag fetch happens back in Decide release, so a tag created on origin in between would be missed, git tag would succeed locally and the push would be rejected as non-fast-forward after a successful publish, which is exactly the npm ahead of git state this work removes. The step now fetches tags and compares against the remote tag target, exiting cleanly when the tag already points at the verified commit. CodeRabbit also found that the dist entry in the verification diff verified nothing, because nothing rebuilds before it so git diff compared dist against itself and always passed, and git diff cannot see untracked or orphaned artifacts. Where dist is tracked the step now rebuilds from clean and uses git status porcelain with untracked files included. Reproducibility was confirmed locally in every repository that tracks dist before shipping the check.

value.author: claude
value.text: CodeRabbit found a security regression in the thread resolution I added. The loop resolved every unresolved review thread on the release pull request, which would also clear a human reviewer's blocking thread and remove exactly the protection required_conversation_resolution provides for release commits. The GraphQL query now selects the first comment's author type and only bot authored threads are resolved. The jq filter was verified against a sample payload containing one bot thread and one human thread, and it returned only the bot thread.

value.author: claude
value.text: Round four review fixes. Greptile found that classifying a review thread by its first comment lets a bot opened thread with a substantive human reply be auto resolved, bypassing the human concern. A thread now counts as advisory only when every comment on it is bot authored, and threads with no comments are excluded. Verified against four thread shapes, all bot, bot then human, human only, and empty, selecting only the all bot thread. CodeRabbit found the dist rebuild check omitted ignored matching so newly generated ignored artifacts under dist would stay hidden.
